Reasoning: Along the thick-line path from P to Q, the grid vertices in order are (1,0) → (1,1) → (2,1) → (2,3) → (0,3) → (0,5) → (2,5) → (2,7) → (5,7) → (5,4) → (2,4). The lengths of the segments are respectively 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3 side lengths of the smallest square, totaling 21 side lengths of the smallest square. Each smallest square side length is 20 cm, so the distance Adam walked is 21 × 20 = 420 cm.

Add the Manhattan lengths of these straight pieces: 1+1+2+2+2+2+2+3+3+3 = 21 smallest-square sides. From the text, one smallest side is 20 cm, so the distance is 21 × 20 = 420 cm.

method.method_draft: Use algebraic square sizes rather than first drawing the whole grid. Let the smallest, medium, and largest square side lengths be S, M, and L. From the image, the height of the upper-right large square equals the top small square plus the upper-left medium square, so L = S + M. Also the full rectangle height can be read on the left as S + 3M, and on the right as L + S + L, so S + 3M = 2L + S. Solving gives M = 2S and L = 3S. Now classify the bold path pieces by square-size edges: it contains 2 small-side pieces, 5 medium-side pieces, and 3 large-side pieces. Thus its length is 2S + 5M + 3L = 2S + 10S + 9S = 21S. The text gives S = 20 cm, so the walk is 21 × 20 = 420 cm.
